proposals.before: When Feng Changqing was recalled to court, Qiyun had himself appointed acting investigating censor and served as army marshal.
proposals.after: When Feng Changqing was recalled to court, he recommended Qiyun as acting investigating censor and army marshal.
proposals.reason: Chinese 常清被召，表攝監察御史 names Changqing as the one recalled; 表 is his memorial recommending Qiyun, not Qiyun appointing himself.

proposals.before: When Changqing was summoned, Qiyun memorialized that he act as investigating censor and served as army marshal.
proposals.after: When Changqing was summoned, he memorialized that Qiyun act as investigating censor and serve as army marshal.
proposals.reason: The silent subject of 表 after 常清被召 is Changqing recommending Qiyun, not Qiyun memorializing for himself.

proposals.before: He traced the circumstances in which each man had been forced into complicity, weighing guilt and mercy by the facts of each case, and gave Xian his full support; Xian came to cherish and forgive him, and his reputation soon eclipsed that of Lü Yin and Cui Qi.
proposals.after: He traced the circumstances in which each man had been forced into complicity, weighing guilt and mercy by the facts of each case, and gave Xian his full support; Xian therefore valued this leniency, and Xian's reputation soon eclipsed that of Lü Yin and Cui Qi.
proposals.reason: 愛恕之 refers to favoring merciful adjudication, not Xian forgiving Qiyun; 譽出呂諲、崔器上 contrasts Xian's lenient fame with those harsh judges.

proposals.before: He was made prefect of Jiangzhou and then promoted in succession to supervising censor.
proposals.after: He was made prefect of Jiangzhou and then promoted in succession to supervising secretary.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is a chancellery supervising secretary, not a censorial office.

proposals.before: He was made prefect of Jiangzhou, then promoted in succession to supervising censor.
proposals.after: He was made prefect of Jiangzhou, then promoted in succession to supervising secretary.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is mistranslated as a censor; it is the supervising secretary of the Chancellery.

proposals.before: At this time Hua Yuan Assistant Commandant Hou Mochen Fu had been appointed Changan Assistant Commandant through the you quota and had to report to the Censorate; Qiyun looked into his background; Fu's expression changed and he could not answer; he then confessed he had been recommended by Xu Hao, Du Ji, and Xue Yong—not truly on outstanding merit.
proposals.after: At this time Hua Yuan Assistant Commandant Hou Mochen Fu had been appointed Chang'an Assistant Commandant through the outstanding-merit quota and had to report to the Censorate; Qiyun looked into his background; Fu's expression changed and he could not answer; he then confessed he had been recommended by Xu Hao, Du Ji, and Xue Yong—not truly on outstanding merit.
proposals.reason: 優 is the outstanding-merit appointment track; rendering it as English “you” is a fused/corrupted word, not a translation of the quota name.

proposals.before: He was posthumously made minister of the Ministry of Personnel, with posthumous title Literary and Offering.
proposals.after: He was posthumously made minister of the Ministry of Personnel, with posthumous title Wenxian (Cultured and Dedicated).
proposals.reason: 文獻 is the posthumous name Wenxian; “Literary and Offering” is a word-for-word calque that does not read as an English posthumous title.

proposals.before: In the second year of Yuanhe, when Du Huangchang left the chancellorship, Jifu was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent Associate Director of the Chancellery.
proposals.after: In the second year of Yuanhe, when Du Huangchang left the chancellorship, Jifu was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent chancellor (tong zhongshu menxia pingzhangshi).
proposals.reason: 同中書門下平章事 is the Tang chancellor title, not Associate Director of the Chancellery.

proposals.before: Pei Jun, as right vice director of the Secretariat with concurrent charge of the Bureau of Revenue, formed a faction to undermine the ruling ministers.
proposals.after: Pei Jun, as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs with concurrent charge of the Bureau of Revenue, formed a faction to undermine the ruling ministers.
proposals.reason: 尚書右僕射 is Right Pushe of the Shangshu Sheng (Department of State Affairs), not of the Secretariat (中書).

proposals.before: Pei Jun, as right vice director of the Secretariat with concurrent charge of the Bureau of Revenue, formed a faction to overturn those in power.
proposals.after: Pei Jun, as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs with concurrent charge of the Bureau of Revenue, formed a faction to overturn those in power.
proposals.reason: The literal line repeats the same office error: 尚書右僕射 is not a Secretariat post.

proposals.before: Jifu also firmly begged to be relieved, recommended Pei Ji to replace him, and was made acting minister of war, concurrent vice director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery, and military commissioner of Huainan.
proposals.after: Jifu also firmly begged to be relieved, recommended Pei Ji to replace him, and was made acting minister of war, concurrent vice director of the Secretariat and chancellor, and military commissioner of Huainan.
proposals.reason: 同中書門下平章事 is again mistranslated as Associate Director of the Chancellery.

proposals.before: Early Han had no more than sixty commanderies, yet under Emperors Wen and Jing good government nearly matched the Three Dynasties; few commanderies did not mean disorder, nor did many commanderies guarantee good government.
proposals.after: Early Han had no more than sixty commanderies, yet under Emperors Wen and Jing good government nearly matched the Three Kings; few commanderies did not mean disorder, nor did many commanderies guarantee good government.
proposals.reason: Chinese 三王 denotes the Three Kings, not the Three Dynasties (三代); the idiomatic English substitutes the wrong classical referent.

proposals.before: Later Hongzheng was appointed acting right vice director of the Secretariat and granted twenty million in cash for his army; Hongzheng said, "What displeases me is not the money but the transfer of the Heyang garrison."
proposals.after: Later Hongzheng was appointed acting right vice director of the Secretariat and granted twenty million in cash for his army; Hongzheng said, "I am not pleased about the transfer of the Heyang army."
proposals.reason: The Chinese 吾未喜於移河陽軍也 states only displeasure at transferring the Heyang army; the idiomatic version invents a contrast with the cash grant.

proposals.before: At his burial the emperor sacrificed with the lesser tai la ritual and posthumously appointed him Minister of Works.
proposals.after: At his burial the emperor sacrificed with the lesser lao (shaolao) offering and posthumously appointed him Minister of Works.
proposals.reason: 少牢 is the lesser animal sacrifice (shaolao); 'tai la' is a corrupted rendering of 太牢/少牢 sacrificial terminology.

proposals.before: Li Yong, courtesy name Jianhou, was a grandnephew of the famous calligrapher Li Yong, who had served as prefect of Beihai.
proposals.after: Li Yong, courtesy name Jianhou, was a grandnephew of Li Yong, prefect of Beihai.
proposals.reason: The Chinese identifies 邕 only as prefect of Beihai; famous calligrapher is not in the source sentence.

proposals.before: When Xianzong came to the throne he became Intendant of the Capital and was promoted to right vice director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: When Xianzong came to the throne he became Intendant of the Capital and was promoted to Right Aide of the Department of State Affairs.
proposals.reason: 尚書右丞 belongs to the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat.

proposals.before: As imperial forces pressed the campaign against Cai, Li Shidao plotted to interfere; Yong stationed twenty thousand troops along the Yan border and supplied them from his own resources without relying on the central government.
proposals.after: As imperial forces pressed the campaign against Cai, Li Shidao plotted to interfere; Yong stationed twenty thousand troops along the Yun border and supplied them from his own resources without relying on the central government.
proposals.reason: 鄆 is Yun, not Yan.

proposals.before: When Chenghui returned to court he repeatedly praised and recommended him; Yong was summoned as vice director of the Chancellery and concurrent Associate Director of the Chancellery.
proposals.after: When Chenghui returned to court he repeatedly praised and recommended him; Yong was summoned as vice director of the Chancellery and concurrent chancellor (joint manager of affairs with the secretariat-chancellery).
proposals.reason: 同中書門下平章事 is the chancellorship title, not a second Chancellery associate-director post.

proposals.before: Once received in audience he exhaustively discussed the treachery of the eunuch Xu Suizhen, then went through denouncing the chancellors, asked to be tried himself, and also memorialized to borrow the postal relay compound to prepare his wedding.
proposals.after: Once received in audience he exhaustively discussed the treachery of the eunuch Xu Suizhen, then went through denouncing the chancellors, asked to be given a trial assignment, and also memorialized to borrow the postal relay compound to prepare his wedding.
proposals.reason: 求自試 means requesting a trial posting, not asking to be put on trial.

proposals.before: During the turmoil over the succession of the Prince of Xiang, as events shifted in Huainan, Gao Pian accepted a false imperial commission; Xi remonstrated bitterly but was not heeded.
proposals.after: During the turmoil of the Prince of Xiang, as events shifted in Huainan, Gao Pian accepted a false imperial commission; Xi remonstrated bitterly but was not heeded.
proposals.reason: 嗣襄王之亂 refers to the Prince of Xiang's usurpation/rebellion, not a succession of that prince.

proposals.before: During the turmoil of the Prince of Xiang's succession, moving about in Huainan, Gao Pian accepted a false commission; Xi remonstrated bitterly but was not heeded.
proposals.after: During the turmoil of the succeeding Prince of Xiang, moving about in Huainan, Gao Pian accepted a false commission; Xi remonstrated bitterly but was not heeded.
proposals.reason: 嗣襄王 is a title-name for the succeeding Prince of Xiang, not 'the Prince of Xiang's succession'.

proposals.before: When the bones are strong in the four limbs, the ruler has loyal ministers—called bone spurs in the throat.
proposals.after: When the bones are strong in the four limbs, the ruler has loyal ministers—called the bone in the throat.
proposals.reason: 骨鯁 names outspoken loyal remonstrators (a bone in the throat), not bone spurs.

proposals.before: Cui Zhaowei had long resented Xi and prompted Liu Chonglu to snatch his appointment edict and weep over it, saying, "Xi harbors treachery, is on familiar terms with the eunuch Yang Fugong, and his younger brother was killed by Shi Bo—he must not serve as chancellor to the Son of Heaven."
proposals.after: Cui Zhaowei had long resented Xi and prompted Liu Chonglu to snatch his appointment edict and weep over it, saying, "Xi harbors treachery, is on familiar terms with the eunuch Yang Fugong, and his younger brother was killed by Shi Pu—he must not serve as chancellor to the Son of Heaven."
proposals.reason: 時溥 is Shi Pu; Bo does not match 溥.
